newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finmin made no deficit forecast - deputies.
newsitem.headline: French finmin made no deficit forecast - deputies.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn made no forecast for the budget deficit during talks with Socialist members of parliament on Tuesday, deputies said on Wednesday.

Daily Liberation reported on Wednesday that Strauss-Kahn had told Socialist members of parliament in a closed-door meeting the public deficit in 1997 was expected to come in between 3.6 and 3.8 percent of gross domestic product.
The finance ministry declined to comment on the report.
But deputies present at the meeting said Strauss-Kahn had not cited any figure for the deficit.

Strauss-Kahn was due to speak to the National Assembly's influential finance committee on July 2 at 1000 GMT and to the committee's counterpart in the Senate, the upper house of parliament, on July 3 at 1000 GMT.
The government is currently awaiting the outcome of an audit of public finances to be presented by the auditors on July 21. Strauss-Kahn said on Tuesday the results would be made public immediately.
